_note: DRAFT guidance. Have KALRO or Mwea extension officers review and correct every entry before real farmers rely on it.

healthy.name: Healthy
healthy.summary: No disease was detected on this leaf.
actions: Keep checking your fields regularly, especially after rain or humid weather.
Check leaves from different parts of the field, not just one plant.
If you are still worried about the plants, ask your extension officer to inspect them.

blast.name: Blast
blast.summary: Rice blast is a fungal disease and one of the most damaging rice diseases in Kenya.
actions: Contact your extension officer or KALRO soon to confirm the diagnosis and get treatment advice.
Avoid applying too much nitrogen fertiliser, which tends to make blast worse.
Keep water management and drainage in good order.
For future seasons, ask about blast-tolerant varieties and clean seed.

brown_spot.name: Brown spot
brown_spot.summary: Brown spot is a fungal disease that shows as brown spots on the leaves. It is more common on stressed or poorly fed crops.
actions: Ask your extension officer to confirm it before you treat.
Feed the crop in a balanced way and avoid water stress.
Use clean, healthy seed and avoid saving seed from infected fields.
Only use a fungicide if an officer confirms it is needed.

bacterial_leaf_blight.name: Bacterial leaf blight
bacterial_leaf_blight.summary: A bacterial disease that makes leaves yellow and dry from the tips and edges. It can spread through water and rain splash.
actions: Ask your extension officer to confirm it. Bacterial diseases are managed differently from fungal ones such as blast.
Avoid applying too much nitrogen fertiliser.
Avoid moving water or tools from affected fields to healthy ones.
Use clean seed and ask about resistant varieties for future seasons.

rice_yellow_mottle_virus.name: Rice yellow mottle virus (RYMV)
rice_yellow_mottle_virus.summary: A viral disease that causes yellowing, mottling and stunting. There is no cure once a plant is infected.
actions: Report it to your extension officer or KALRO so it can be confirmed and tracked.
Remove badly affected plants if an officer advises it, so the virus spreads less.
Keep weeds and volunteer rice under control, because they can carry the virus.
Avoid working through infected plants and then through healthy ones.
Ask about resistant varieties for future seasons.
